<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I understand the request. I am planning the implementation steps.

The plan breaks down into three parts. A manual tree builder will let users draw split thresholds and rebuild the tree interactively. An interactive scatter plot will support drag-to-place split lines and highlight leaf regions. A new overlay component will pair the scatter plot with the live tree visualization.

The overlay will include controls to choose the split axis, drag a threshold line, and undo or reset splits. Users can click a leaf region to trigger a new split, toggling between vertical and horizontal modes. The tree updates live as each boundary is drawn.

The interaction will use a simpler flow. The current node defaults to the root. Users toggle between vertical and horizontal axes. They drag a line on the scatter plot to set the threshold. Releasing the mouse confirms the split and rebuilds the tree.

I am designing the underlying data structures. A manual split will record the target node, axis, and threshold. The tree state will use a recursive structure to represent leaves and internal nodes.

I am deciding between two implementation strategies. One stores each split as an edit and rebuilds the tree from samples. The other maintains a live tree and replaces a leaf with a decision node when the user commits a split. I will use the latter approach.

I am now writing the `manualTree.ts` module. It defines `createManualTreeRoot` to initialize the tree from a full sample set. It defines `applySplit` to find a leaf node, verify it contains impure samples, partition the data, and replace the leaf with a decision node.

I will track which samples belong to each node so splits partition correctly within a leaf's region. Clicking tree nodes will select the next target for splitting. I am now starting the `InteractiveSplitPlot.tsx` component.

The scatter plot will display samples, leaf regions, and existing splits. Users can drag a preview line to set a threshold, then release to commit the split. This button will appear only in fullscreen mode, placed in the same action toolbar used for the other training options.

I will place the Train yourself button in the expand overlay's header or toolbar rather than the main explore toolbar. I am also checking the scatter plot CSS to style the draggable split lines.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have a clear plan and am beginning implementation.

Implementation will touch four files. A new manual tree module will handle split logic and sample collection. An interactive plot component will support drag-to-split. A training overlay UI will provide the interface. The forest demo will gain state and a fullscreen button to trigger it. The manual tree API will collect samples by node region and apply splits to leaves.

The manual tree API now includes `splitLeaf`, `createEmptyManualTree`, `findSplittableLeaves`, and `isValidSplit`. These functions handle splitting leaves, initializing the root, finding nodes ready to split, and validating that both child regions contain at least one sample.

A recursive `walk` function will traverse the tree to collect samples for a specific node. It filters samples against each split threshold along the path and recurses into the matching child until reaching the target leaf.

The recursive `walk` function now branches into the correct child based on whether each sample falls below or above the current split threshold. Next, `splitLeaf` will deep clone the tree and replace the target leaf with two new children.

`splitLeaf` now validates that both child regions contain at least one sample before splitting. It begins a recursive `replace` function to clone the tree and insert the new split node.

The recursive `replace` function now builds decision nodes with new leaf children. Leaf IDs may change during splits, so selected-node tracking needs adjustment. A history stack will support undo. The interactive plot UX is next.

The interactive plot will let users select a leaf region by clicking its tinted area or tree node. They then choose a split axis—Width or Length—and drag a line across the region. Valid splits commit on mouse up. While dragging, the preview line and point highlights update live. The component will use SVG drag handlers and detect leaf regions for selection.

Clicks inside leaf regions will select the containing leaf. Undo and reset buttons will be added. Max depth will come from the ForestDemo config. The overlay will layer on top of fullscreen mode with z-index 90.

The Train Yourself button will appear only in the fullscreen expand overlay toolbar, not the main action bar. It will layer on top of the forest behind it, similar to the Train Forest overlay. The interactive plot component will convert mouse coordinates into data space using fixed dimensions and padding.

Data-space coordinate conversion is now defined. Mouse X maps to X via `fromX` and Y via `fromY`. During a drag, the threshold snaps to the nearest pixel value and clamps to the leaf region bounds.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Added a **Train yourself** mode in fullscreen. Here’s how it works:

### How to use it
1. Enter **Explore** mode and click **↗** to open the full forest view.
2. Click **Train yourself** in the toolbar.
3. In the interactive lab:
   - **Click a mixed-color region** (or a leaf in the tree) to select it.
   - Choose **Leaf width** (vertical line) or **Leaf length** (horizontal line).
   - **Drag** inside the region to draw a boundary — points preview left/right as you drag.
   - Release to commit the split; the tree updates immediately.
4. Repeat on other regions until the tree is fully split, or use **Undo split** / **Reset**.

### What was built
- **`TrainYourselfOverlay`** — interactive lab with scatter plot + live tree view
- **`InteractiveSplitPlot`** — click-to-select regions, drag-to-draw split lines with live point preview
- **`lib/forest/manualTree.ts`** — manual tree building from your boundaries (validates splits, tracks history)

The tree respects your current **max depth** setting from the forest knobs. Pure regions (single class) can’t be split further — pick another mixed region to keep going.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Fixed. There were two bugs causing the flaky behavior:

1. **Drag was required** — splits only committed if you moved the mouse, so a plain click did nothing.
2. **Stale selection** — the split used the previously selected region, not the one you clicked, because React state hadn't updated yet.

**Now:**
- **Single click** places the line at that spot (snapped to the nearest valid split between points).
- **Hover** still previews the line before you click.
- The clicked region is passed directly into the split, so there's no selection lag.

Pure regions still won't split (there's nothing to separate) — click a mixed-color area instead.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The maximum depth limit of 3 was blocking further splits after two levels.

Click placement and axis hints were also improved.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

The orange tint was a red herring — the real blocker was **max depth**.

Manual training was using the forest's `maxDepth: 3`, which silently blocked any split after **2 levels** (`depth >= 2` couldn't split). So once you had three regions, deeper ones were dead — regardless of color.

**Fixed:**
1. **Removed the depth limit** from manual training — you can keep splitting as long as a region has 2+ points
2. **Click placement** now uses your exact click position (when valid), not only midpoints between points
3. **Axis hint** — if width splits aren't possible (all points share the same width), the status bar tells you to press **D** or **L** to split on length instead

Region color is just the majority vote label — it never blocked splits. You should be able to keep carving up any orange (or any color) region now.
